transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I’m here because people keep telling me I’m making too much of things, and I don’t want to sound unreasonable, doctor. But I know what I’m seeing.

My wife’s relative has been coming into the house to get at me. My tools don’t just move around by themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get messed up every single weekend by accident. It’s been going on for months, and to me it’s pretty plain he’s trying to take over my place and push me out.
Do you think there's any possibility that you might be mistaken about your wife's relative trying to take over your place?

I mean… I don’t want to come across like I’m being stubborn, doctor, and sure, I suppose anybody can be wrong about some little thing. But this isn’t just one little thing.

Everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know what’s been happening. My wife’s relative came into the house to get at me. My tools don’t just move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend. After all these months, it’s plain as day to me he’s trying to take over my place and push me out.
Do you think there's anything that could ever change your mind about your wife's relative trying to take over your place?

I don’t want to sound closed-minded, doctor. I know you’re asking a fair question. But… honestly, I don’t know what would change my mind at this point.

Everybody keeps saying I’m imagining it, but my tools don’t just move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get spoiled every weekend for no reason. After all these months, it’s just plain to me that he came into the house to get at me and he’s trying to take over my place, push me out. I’m not trying to be difficult—I just know what I’ve seen.
Have you ever had any doubts about your belief that your wife's relative is trying to take over your place?

I’ve tried to give it some thought, doctor, because I don’t want you thinking I’m just being unreasonable. Maybe at the very beginning I wondered if I was making too much of it.

But after all these months… no, not really. Everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative came into the house to get at me. My tools don’t move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get spoiled every weekend by accident. It’s plain to me he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.
Is your belief that your wife's relative is trying to take over your place part of a larger plan or scheme that you've figured out?

I don’t know if I’d call it a big scheme, doctor… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound more dramatic than it is. But it does feel connected.

It’s not just one thing. My wife’s relative came into the house, and since then it’s been my tools getting moved, my fishing plans getting ruined every weekend… little things that maybe someone else would brush off, but after months of it, it adds up. To me it’s plain he’s trying to get at me, take over my place, and push me out. I hope that makes sense.
Do you think your wife's relative is working alone to take over your place?

I… I don’t know that I’d say he’s got people working with him, doctor. I don’t want to accuse anybody else if I can’t prove it.

What I do know is, since he came into the house, things haven’t been right. My tools don’t just move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get spoiled every weekend by accident. After all these months, it feels plain to me he’s trying to get at me, take over my place, and push me out. If that sounds too strong, I’m sorry, but that’s how it looks to me.
Do you think your wife's relative's actions against you are part of an organized plan?

I don’t want to make it sound like some big organized thing if that sounds… I don’t know, unreasonable. But it does feel like there’s a pattern to it.

Everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, and that’s why I’m here, I guess. But I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. My tools don’t move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend. After all these months, it’s plain as day to me he’s trying to take over my place and push me out.

I’m not saying I know every detail of a plan, doctor, but it doesn’t feel random.
Do you think there are other people who believe your wife's relative is trying to take over your place?

I’m not sure other people would say it the way I do, doctor. Most of them act like I’m imagining it, and that’s… that’s part of why I’m here, I guess.

But I know what I’m seeing. Since my wife’s relative came into the house, my tools don’t just move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get spoiled every weekend by accident. After all these months, it’s plain to me he’s trying to get at me, take over my place, and push me out.

I don’t know if anyone else believes it exactly, but I wish they’d at least see what I’m talking about.
How long have you believed that your wife's relative is trying to take over your place?

It’s been… about nine months, I’d say. Since my wife’s relative moved into our home. I don’t want to make it sound like I’ve been keeping some exact calendar or anything, but that’s when I started feeling like he was trying to take over my place.
Do you think your wife's relative's actions against you are all part of a single, coherent plan?

I mean… “single, coherent plan” sounds pretty strong, doctor, and I don’t want to come off like I’m making it bigger than it is. But yes, to me it fits together.

I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. My tools don’t move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend. After all these months, it’s hard not to see it as him trying to take over my place and push me out. Does that make sense?
Do you think there are other people or forces involved in trying to harm you or control your life, beyond just your wife's relative?

No… I don’t think it’s, you know, some big group or anything like that. I don’t want to sound unreasonable.

It’s really him—my wife’s relative. I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know he came into the house to get at me. My tools don’t move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get spoiled every weekend by accident. After all these months, it just seems plain to me he’s trying to take over my place and push me out. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you think your belief about your wife's relative will ever change?

I’d like to say it could change, if that’s the right answer… I don’t want to seem stubborn. But honestly, doctor, I don’t see how I’m supposed to just stop believing what I can see happening.

I’m here because everyone keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative came into the house to get at me. My tools don’t move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get ruined by accident every weekend. After all these months, it’s plain to me he’s trying to take over my place and push me out.

So… unless something really showed me otherwise, I don’t think that belief is going to change.
Do you think there's anything that could happen that would make you question your entire understanding of what's going on with your wife's relative?

I mean… I suppose if there was some real explanation, something that actually made sense of all of it, I’d have to listen. I don’t want to be the kind of person who won’t even consider it.

But it would have to explain a lot, doctor. I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, and I know what that sounds like, but I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. My tools don’t just move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t keep getting spoiled every weekend by accident.

After all these months, it looks plain as day to me that he’s trying to take over my place and push me out. So… yes, maybe something could make me question it, but it would have to be something pretty clear. Does that make sense?
Do you think your wife's relative is the only person who knows about his plan to take over your place?

I… I don’t really know who he’s told, if that’s what you mean. I don’t want to make it sound bigger than it is.

What I know is him. I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me—my tools don’t move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t keep getting spoiled by accident every weekend. After all these months, it’s plain to me he’s trying to take over my place and push me out.

Whether he’s keeping that to himself or talking to somebody else… I can’t say for sure. Is that an okay way to answer?
Do you think your wife's relative has a specific goal in mind for taking over your place?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, doctor, like I’ve got some big story worked out, but it feels pretty clear to me that he wants me out of my own place.

I’m here because everybody keeps saying I’m imagining it, and I get how that sounds, but I know he came into this house to get at me. My tools don’t move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t keep getting ruined every weekend for no reason.

After all these months, it seems plain as day that the goal is to take over my place and push me out. I mean… that’s what it looks like to me. Is that answering what you mean?
Do you think your wife's relative has a well-thought-out plan for taking over your place, or is it more of a spontaneous thing?

I don’t know if I’d call it “well-thought-out,” exactly… I don’t want to make it sound like I’m saying he’s got some written plan or anything like that.

But it doesn’t feel spontaneous to me. Not after all these months. I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know he came into this house to get at me. My tools don’t just move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get spoiled every weekend by accident.

So… whether he planned every step or he’s just taking chances as they come, I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out. Is that what you mean?
Do you think your wife's relative is carefully planning each step to take over your place?

I… I don’t know if I can say he’s carefully planning every single step. I don’t want to overstate it or sound like I’m making something up.

But I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, and I know what’s been happening. He came into this house to get at me. My tools don’t move themselves, my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend, and after all these months… I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.

So maybe I can’t prove each step is planned, doctor, but it sure doesn’t feel random to me. Is that a fair way to put it?
For how long have you held this belief about your wife's relative trying to take over your place?

It’s been… about nine months, I guess. Since he moved into our home.

I don’t want to make it sound like I was counting the days or anything, but that’s when I started feeling this way about it. Around then. Does that make sense?
Do you think there's anything about your wife's relative that could change and make you no longer believe he's trying to take over your place?

I mean… I’d like to think so, doctor. I don’t want to sound like I’m completely unwilling to listen or anything.

But honestly, after all these months, I don’t know what he could change that would make me just stop believing it. My tools don’t move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get spoiled every weekend by accident. I’m here because everyone keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know he came into this house to get at me.

If he stopped pushing into my space and trying to take over my place, maybe that would matter… but right now, I can see it pretty plainly. Does that answer what you mean?

target_item.manifestation: I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me—my tools don’t move themselves, my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend, and after all these months I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the structure and intentionality of the patient's fixed belief that his wife's relative is planning to take over his place, which directly concerns the delusional belief.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I’d call it “well-thought-out,” exactly… I don’t want to make it sound like I’m saying he’s got some written plan or anything like that.

But it doesn’t feel spontaneous to me. Not after all these months. I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know he came into this house to get at me. My tools don’t just move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get spoiled every weekend by accident.

So… whether he planned every step or he’s just taking chances as they come, I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out. Is that what you mean?

doctor.intent: determine the level of organization in the patient's delusional beliefs
doctor.question: Do you think your wife's relative is carefully planning each step to take over your place?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me—my tools don’t move themselves, my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend, and after all these months I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.
target_item.reason: The question asks about the patient's fixed belief that his wife's relative is planning to take over his place, specifically whether the relative is carefully planning each step.

patient.answer:
I… I don’t know if I can say he’s carefully planning every single step. I don’t want to overstate it or sound like I’m making something up.

But I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, and I know what’s been happening. He came into this house to get at me. My tools don’t move themselves, my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend, and after all these months… I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.

So maybe I can’t prove each step is planned, doctor, but it sure doesn’t feel random to me. Is that a fair way to put it?

doctor.intent: Determine the duration of the patient's delusional belief
doctor.question: For how long have you held this belief about your wife's relative trying to take over your place?

target_item.name: Duration
target_item.manifestation: This has been going on for about nine months, ever since my wife’s relative moved into our home.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking how long the belief has been held, which directly corresponds to the duration of the delusional belief.

patient.answer:
It’s been… about nine months, I guess. Since he moved into our home.

I don’t want to make it sound like I was counting the days or anything, but that’s when I started feeling this way about it. Around then. Does that make sense?

doctor.intent: determine the presence of a fixed delusional system
doctor.question: Do you think there's anything about your wife's relative that could change and make you no longer believe he's trying to take over your place?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me—my tools don’t move themselves, my fishing plans don’t get spoiled by accident every weekend, and after all these months I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about whether the belief could change in response to new circumstances or evidence, which directly concerns the fixed nature of the delusion.

patient.answer:
I mean… I’d like to think so, doctor. I don’t want to sound like I’m completely unwilling to listen or anything.

But honestly, after all these months, I don’t know what he could change that would make me just stop believing it. My tools don’t move themselves, and my fishing plans don’t get spoiled every weekend by accident. I’m here because everyone keeps acting like I’m imagining it, but I know he came into this house to get at me.

If he stopped pushing into my space and trying to take over my place, maybe that would matter… but right now, I can see it pretty plainly. Does that answer what you mean?

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's persistent belief that his wife's relative is trying to take over his place, despite lack of evidence and others' skepticism, suggests a delusional disorder. The belief is non-bizarre, persistent, and not part of a larger psychotic syndrome, which aligns with F22 (Delusional disorder).
